6\. Research Archive: PC + Research Table + Field Guide Sync Loop (Sept 2026, new)

LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): the Research Station (Part 6) can hold a dedicated Field Guide slot alongside its existing PC and research interface. Insert the guide, and the table can READ existing entries, add newly-generated research, complete incomplete entries, and unlock new sections; take the guide back out and the updates travel with the player. This makes the three pieces a genuine three-way loop rather than separate mechanics: PC answers 'who/what do I have,' the Research Table answers 'what can I investigate,' the Field Guide answers 'what do I actually know.' A Pokemon assigned to research does not need to physically leave the PC — the table establishes a research LINK to it rather than requiring removal, so the player's active party stays independent of what's being studied.

*Research is not necessarily fully automated by the table either: a research subject can have explicit required observations (night exposure, moonlight exposure, a specific Ball's resonance, a friendship threshold) that only get satisfied by the player actually doing them in the field — the table can report 'additional field observations required' rather than silently completing everything itself, keeping research an actual activity rather than an idle-game timer.*

7\. Research Access Pacing (Sept 2026, new)

LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): research capability should expand horizontally and ramp up WITH the player from early game, not arrive as a late-game unlock — explicit design goal, stated directly: don't let the choice to disengage from research be caused by lack of early access rather than genuine player preference. Rough progression: Field Guide arrives early (basic identification/observation, understands little yet) → early-mid PC+Guide synchronization (ownership data starts feeding the guide) → mid-game Research/Analysis Table (active investigation) → mid-late PC integration (select specific stored Pokemon for research) → late advanced research modules (cross-species comparison, specialized phenomena) → endgame full research network (automated/long-term studies). Framed as accumulating CAPABILITIES rather than grinding a research XP bar.

*Hard rule: never gate basic knowledge-recording behind the Research Table itself. A player who encounters something interesting in the wild should be able to record SOMETHING in their Field Guide immediately regardless of what infrastructure they've built — the Table makes research faster/more thorough, it is not the only entry point to the whole system. That preserves genuine player choice (ignoring the advanced machinery is a legitimate playstyle) without that choice being an artifact of the game introducing the system too late to matter.*

8\. ChatGPT Import Integration Pass (Sept 2026) — Research System Charter, Progression Backbone, Camera/Namespace Resolutions

LOCKED (cross-checked and adopted from a parallel Claude session's integration pass over a large ChatGPT conversation batch, largely covering the same material already processed this session but adding several genuinely new architectural resolutions): a consistent set of proposals resolving redundancy clusters that had built up across many separate mod-research threads. Adopted as follows.

Research System Charter: four systems each own a distinct slice of 'research' rather than competing — Cobblemon Snap owns photographic/observational research (encounter, photograph, pose, activity, habitat, Snapdex progression); Cobblemon Research Tasks owns active/interactive research (catching, battling, breeding, evolving, item/move use — things done TO or WITH the Pokemon rather than observed); the Field Journal (custom, built atop both) owns the narrative layer (player notes, favorite photos, discovered lore, world/biome context); FTB Quests owns the campaign/expedition layer (multi-step story content not tied to a single species). The already-locked Field Guide UI (Part 12/13 area) becomes the single front-end window into all four rather than an implementation of any of them itself.

*Field Guide (the mod) discovery-trigger split — SUPERSEDED, see the Three-Path Research Architecture entry immediately below. The original binary version (spyglass for world, Pokedex-scan-only for Pokemon, with Pokemon explicitly EXCLUDED from spyglass discovery) is kept here for record but is no longer the design — Wesley refined it into a genuinely stronger model the same session.*

*Three-Path Research Architecture, LOCKED (Sept 2026, Wesley): resolves the discovery-trigger question by turning it into a PLAYSTYLE choice rather than a mandatory per-category rule. Three distinct research paths, each with its own tool/trigger and its own presentation, all writing into the exact same underlying Field Guide unlock state — one shared foundation, not three parallel databases. Explorer path: spyglass, Field Guide's native mechanic, unchanged and left fully intact (including for Pokemon — the earlier exclusion is reversed). Trainer path: Cobblemon Pokedex scan event, bridged via KubeJS calling Field Guide's unlock command (implementation steps unchanged from the prior entry — still needs the exact unlock-command syntax, the exact scan-event name, and the species-ID→entry-ID mapping confirmed before the listener is written). Photographer path: Cobblemon Snap's photograph-taken event, also bridged via KubeJS into the same unlock command — a fourth trigger-path element not previously scoped, requiring the same verification-before-building discipline (confirm Snap's actual exposed photo-taken event/KubeJS hook before assuming one exists in the form needed). Whichever path a player favors, discovering a Pokemon through ANY of the three marks it discovered for that player system-wide — no duplicate re-discovery required across paths, and a player is never forced to carry a tool that doesn't match how they actually like to play.*

*Presentation-layer distinction proposed, not yet built: the three triggers can read differently at the moment of discovery (scan reticle vs. Pokedex animation vs. camera flash) without requiring separate data structures, since only the trigger differs — the unlock write is identical regardless of path. A natural extension, consistent with the already-locked Field Guide visual grammar rule ('Photograph = player's actual observation'): a Photographer-path discovery could populate the entry with the player's own Snap photo, while Explorer/Trainer-path discoveries use the default sprite/silhouette treatment — giving each path a genuinely different resulting entry, not just a different button press, without inventing new mechanics beyond what's already locked.*

Progression backbone unification: ProgressiveStages is the single source of truth for 'what has this player unlocked' — RCT's trainer level-cap triggers and any custom Route Mode gate WRITE TO ProgressiveStages flags on completion rather than keeping independent state, so quests/recipes/world-access checks all read from one stage graph instead of three systems potentially disagreeing about what a player has earned.

Two-camera resolution, confirmed rather than newly proposed — matches this archive's own already-locked camera split: Cobblemon Snap's camera is the field-research instrument (owns the Field Guide's photographic evidence per the Charter above); Exposure is the personal/artistic instrument (scenery, printable physical photographs, camera stands, developing, no research scoring). A third 'generic handheld camera' placeholder from earlier in that conversation's history is explicitly retired as redundant once Snap's actual camera was found to already cover that role.

cer: adopted as the single canonical namespace for all custom content, replacing two competing candidates (cobblemon_er, er) that arose in different parts of the same conversation without either being formally chosen — short, unambiguous, matches the project's own C.E.R. abbreviation.

*Implementation Layer Principle proposed as a governance addition (not yet formally cross-referenced against this archive's existing Bridge-Eligible Mod / Mental Economy Delegation / Integration Depth Tiers / Synergy Combos principles, but consistent with all four): content and rules (recipes, loot, advancements, tags, simple progression) belong in the datapack layer; new capability (blocks, entities, GUIs, rendering, persistent state machines) belongs in a mod; cross-mod glue and scripted behavior belong in KubeJS; presentation-only changes belong in the resource pack. Never drop to a lower layer merely because it's technically possible.*

*Route Mode: confirmed via fresh research that a real 'Routes' mod exists (road-generation, not progression-gating — signposted terrain-aware roads connecting structures, Xaero's/Waystones integration, purely cosmetic/optional) and that Cobblemon Nuzlocke Mode is a real precedent for the opt-in-toggle UX pattern being proposed, but NO pre-made mod does sequential route-by-route progression gating. Proposed as a small custom build, not a mod search: Routes supplies the physical road geography for free; a custom opt-in Route Mode toggle (styled after Nuzlocke Mode's own \`/command config\` and \`/command status\` UX, off by default, per-player, saved) rides on infrastructure already committed to — ProgressiveStages owns which route is unlocked, RCT's key-trainer defeat (or a research/Titan gate for non-battle routes) triggers the unlock. A player who never touches the toggle plays completely free-roam exactly as today; the toggle only changes whether the game checks the flag before letting the player leave a route's bounds.*

*Biosphere access reframed into a primary/secondary split rather than one dimension with two competing lore explanations: primary access is a Threshold Anchor built via Affinity research at a detected corruption/quarantine site (the 'real' mechanism, tied directly to the already-locked corruption/restoration progression); secondary/flavor access is a Dream Echo obtainable through Psychic-affinity research (Munna/Musharna specifically) — a temporary, unstable, vision-like partial view into a Biosphere, available earlier but less complete than a proper Threshold Anchor. Preserves the dream-world idea as an earlygame teaser without making napping the load-bearing explanation for how a scientific quarantine dimension is entered.*

*Lost Mob Grinders and Lost Biomes unified as artifacts and casualties of the SAME historical corruption event, rather than two unrelated 'ancient ruins' flavors — recovering a Lost Mob Grinder and researching a quarantined biome become two entry points into one overarching mystery.*

*Pokebelt dropped in favor of reskinning a Vanilla Backport Bundle as a 'Trainer's Belt' (custom texture + name only) — gets the trainer-belt fantasy with zero new dependencies and zero loader-compatibility risk, since Pokebelt's Fabric-only status was never resolved to a native NeoForge port.*

*Vanilla Backport's bundled Chaos Cubed/Sulfur/Cinnabar content (confirmed elsewhere in this archive as NOT actually a vanilla backport, but bonus content riding in the same jar) should be logged as a separate, independently removable M.M.I. entry from the genuine vanilla-content half, so a future Mod Audit can drop one without re-litigating the other.*

*Remote Access-style dynamic multiblock GUI (the Tinkers-table laboratory concept) downgraded from 'system we're building' to an explicit stretch goal — dynamically detecting nearby blocks and merging their capabilities into one contextual GUI is genuine custom mod development, not a datapack-reachable feature and not something KubeJS's current GUI hooks reliably support. Laboratory blocks should be designed to work fine as separate, individually-opened machines first; the unified GUI layer is a nice-to-have added later if the tooling exists.*

*Affinity biome-distribution weighting should be built on true vanilla/common biome tags (temperature/forest/cold classifications) rather than depending on Vanilla Backport's specific tag namespace for the same categories — keeps the core Affinity system decoupled from a content mod that could be partially removed in a future audit.*

## C. Master Archive Part 4

Cobblemon: Ecological Resonance

Master Archive — Part 4: Mods, Architecture, Progression Philosophy & Core Fantasy

*Compiled by Claude, September 2026, under Free Reign Mode / TriSweep. Final installment of the Master Archive: the tech/magic mod pillars, world generation approach, technical architecture and spawn pipeline, progression/quest philosophy, the core gameplay loop and player fantasy, the project's own design backlog, and a consolidated mod list including today's additions (Cobblemon Cards, Synchro Machine, Stone Statues).*

1\. The Three Pillars, Restated

Life (Cobblemon, ecosystems, flora, exploration, research, restoration), Industry (Create, infrastructure, engineering, transportation, sustainable automation), and Magic (Ars Nouveau, Occultism, potentially Malum; natural and forbidden magic) — the explicit goal is for these three to interact with each other rather than read as three separate modpacks bolted together, mediated through the Restoration Engine (Part 1) and Nature's Aura (below).

2\. The Magic Trio

|               |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|---------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Mod**       | **Role**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Nature's Aura | Natural/ecological magic — the physical natural-energy substrate underneath the whole ecological system (see Part 1). Confirmed 1.21.1 NeoForge support checked directly against the mod's actual current version rather than assumed.                           |
| Ars Nouveau   | Personal spellcraft/magical creation — customizable spells, magical artifacts, rituals, magical automation. Potential role: Magic / Research / Resonance manipulation.                                                                                           |
| Occultism     | Ritual/spirit/automation magic — spirits, familiars, dimensional/ritual systems, storage. A deliberately different identity from Ars Nouveau so the two don't overlap.                                                                                           |
| Ars Ocultas   | The bridge mod between Ars Nouveau and Occultism — strongly recommended IF both of the above are kept, per the project's general integration philosophy: favor bridge mods that make two systems feel like one world rather than leaving them as isolated silos. |

Malum was named as a 'later' consideration — interesting, but not necessary for establishing the core architecture, and explicitly deferred rather than rejected. Status: 🟢 Strong reconstruction for Nature's Aura/Ars Nouveau/Occultism/Ars Ocultas as the core magic stack; 🟡 Candidate for Malum.

3\. Industry & Community

Create is the physical-infrastructure pillar — explicitly meant to visibly restore civilization (railways, factories, workshops, transportation, power/processing) rather than just being “craft machine, get reward.” Paired with the Sustainable Industry idea from Part 1 (industrial activity should be able to affect Nature's Aura and local affinities, not just extract resources for free).

Farmer's Delight expands farming/cooking/food prep and was floated as a natural future Affinity-activity source (cultivation → ecological effects) without committing to the specifics yet. Supplementaries (jars, signposts, faucets, planters, small decoration/automation) was specifically recommended for making restored villages/factions/settlements feel lived-in, tying directly into the Resonance Ecology building-lifecycle concept from Part 1. Quark was floated as a configurable vanilla+ option, with an explicit caveat to review its config carefully rather than enabling it wholesale. Status: 🟢 Strong reconstruction for Create/Farmer's Delight/Supplementaries' roles; 🟡 Candidate for Quark.

4\. World Generation

Potential environmental stack named: Terralith, Regions Unexplored, Nature's Spirit, Towns & Towers, YUNG's structure mods, and related ecology/structure mods. Explicit governing rule, worth preserving verbatim in spirit: a biome or structure mod is only worth keeping if it contributes to the Living World premise — curate rather than blindly enable everything, and a mod (Regions Unexplored was the specific example given) is never automatically sacred to the pack just because it's aesthetically liked; gate, remove, or replace any piece that doesn't fit the restoration/ecology model. Status: 🟡 Candidate list, 🕒 Locked curation philosophy.

5\. Technical Architecture

Confirmed target: Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge. Core architecture relies on Cobblemon's native systems, datapacks, KubeJS, and custom scripts/persistent player and world state — explicit design principle: mods provide mechanics, the Restoration Engine connects those mechanics into one world (see Part 1).

|                |                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Data scope** | **Illustrative fields**                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Player data    | starter, generations\[\], personal_affinity\[\], active_affinities\[\], dormant_affinities\[\], resonance\[\], hearts, virtues\[\], faction_reputation\[\], owned/caught Pokémon, research, discoveries |
| World data     | world_affinity\[\], ecological_state, natural_aura_state, building_state, population, faction_state, corruption, events, legendary_state                                                                |

Spawn Engine

Native Cobblemon spawning provides the foundation; the custom Restoration Engine layer determines eligibility on top of it. Pipeline: Cobblemon Spawn → Restoration Engine check → Generation unlocked? → World Affinity sufficient? → Ecology state appropriate? → Habitat match? → Dual-type compatibility (Part 1's affinity-closeness rule)? → Regional conditions? → Special event active? → Eligible to spawn. This sits above, not instead of, Cobblemon's normal habitat/spawn rules — confirmed technically plausible via Cobblemon's actual spawn-rule and spawn-pool systems, which support exactly this kind of global weight modification and filtering. Status: 🕒 Locked for the overall architecture shape; implementation specifics (exact KubeJS hooks, data schema) are 🟡 unbuilt.

6\. Progression Philosophy

Seven progression categories, deliberately overlapping rather than siloed: Quest (someone gives you a goal), Advancement (you accomplished something), Discovery (you found something unknown), Event (the world reacts), Miracle (something beneficial and extraordinary happened — escalating Miracle → Great Miracle → World Miracle), Anomaly (something unusual/dangerous happened — escalating Anomaly → Severe Anomaly → Disaster), and Hidden (a system was operating beneath the surface). Illustrative target balance: ~40% structured progression (FTB Quests-style), 25% exploration/discovery, 25% emergent events, 10% hidden systems — explicitly not literal playtime requirements, more a design-emphasis guide. Underlying philosophy, worth keeping verbatim: quests give confidence, advancements give satisfaction, discovery gives curiosity, events give surprise, hidden systems give depth. Status: 🟢 Strong reconstruction.

7\. The Core Gameplay Loop

The whole modpack reduced to one loop: Explore → Observe → Photograph → Research → Discover → Restore → World becomes healthier → Flora + Pokémon return → New places/species → New discoveries → Explore (repeat). Underneath it, the Restoration Engine connects Affinity, Ecology, and Factions into one Living World (Pokémon, Flora, People), which eventually feeds into Legendary Recognition → Domain Authority → the World's True History → the Ancient Threat → the story's second act (Part 1's Act I/II/III structure).

The Core Player Fantasy

Given as an explicit emotional progression the design should protect, worth preserving in the project's own words rather than paraphrased: it should feel like arriving in a broken world and bringing something back everywhere you go; then that the things you're restoring are beginning to notice you; then that the Pokémon aren't just appearing, they're responding; then that something ancient has noticed what you're doing; and eventually the reveal that you thought you were restoring the world, but you were reopening it. Status: 🕒 Locked — explicitly flagged as the identity to protect through future design work.

Multiplayer & Replayability

World Affinity is shared server-wide; Personal Affinity is per-player, so one player can specialize Fire while another specializes Water and both contribute to the same world's restoration. Different playthroughs are meant to diverge meaningfully via starter choice, generation unlock order, personal affinity build, faction alignment, Legendary recognition order, virtue development, and Fusion/Shadow discoveries — explicitly a major design goal, not an incidental side effect.

8\. The Project's Own Design Backlog

Preserved close to verbatim because it's genuinely useful as your own planning reference, not just archive material — this reflects the state of the backlog at the mid-project consolidation checkpoint (Part 3's note applies: some items below were resolved later elsewhere in the transcripts, e.g. Retirement/Championship Protocols, the 10 material families, and Twisted Forms all now have full designs in Parts 1–3 above).

Deliberately NOT added (avoid over-systematizing)

- Dozens of individual meters; a separate Shadow Affinity stat; a separate Fusion Affinity stat; separate Fakemon progression; separate regional-form progression; separate ecological energy currency

- Permanent Fusion failure penalties; excessive daily building-maintenance chores; constant negative affinity loss; huge numbers of Legendary requirements; a dedicated quest for every single emergent event

Circle-back list (as of the consolidation checkpoint)

High priority: Nature's Aura integration specifics, Ecological Health/Nature mechanics, exact World Affinity progression stages, Generation progression rules, Legendary recognition architecture (Pokémon → Virtue Pool → Domain → Signs → Recognition), Fusion compatibility matrix, Shadow creation mechanics, Fakemon implementation specifics — note several of these are now resolved above (Twisted Forms, materials, Fusion safety rules).

Medium priority: EV/IV systems, faction territory evolution, the guard battle system, Domain Authority implementation, sustainable industry mechanics, advanced building-population behavior, regional-variant discovery.

Fun/optional: Plushlocke, Gaucho challenges, the Battle Hall, multiplayer trade challenges, the Golden Plush system — now designed in full in Part 2.

Explicitly deferred to “later” rather than core architecture: Malum, advanced Legendary domain combinations, resurrection mechanics (especially anything requiring Xerneas+Yveltal+Giratina), controlled/intentional Shadow research, and Fusion-born Fakemon — the stated rule was to get ordinary Shadow and ordinary Fusion feeling good on their own before building on top of them.

10\. Crafting Removal — the Production Philosophy Behind C.O.C.

Recovered via the parallel full-sweep pass; this looks like it may be the actual origin point of C.O.C. rather than just another application of it. Explicit goal, in Wesley's own words: remove hand assembly via the 3×3 grid as the default production method — not remove crafting/creation itself.

Proposed hard rule: the 3×3 crafting table becomes an early-game emergency tool at most, largely replaced for real progression recipes. The player still gathers, processes, smelts, mills, presses, infuses, enchants, brews, transmutes, ritualizes, engineers, synthesizes, and automates — just not “combine 6 things in a grid, receive a finished machine.” Create becomes the backbone of physical manufacturing (raw material → processing → components → assembly via Mechanical Crafters/Deployers/Presses/Sequenced Assembly → finished product); Ars Nouveau's enchanting apparatus and Occultism's rituals are named as equally legitimate creation methods alongside Create. AE2/Refined Storage (Section 9 above) handles bulk auto-crafting once a recipe is actually known, rather than the player hand-assembling at scale. Status: 🟡 Candidate — a significant production-philosophy shift, not yet finalized.

11\. Hostile Mobs & Boss Philosophy

Recommendation: keep vanilla hostile mobs, add a small number of highly curated bosses, skip a large boss-mod catalog. Ender's Cataclysm specifically discussed and leaned against — not because its bosses are poorly made, but because a boss with no answer to “what does this mean in our world?” dilutes the pack's identity rather than reinforcing it.

Region-based danger tiers, giving hostile-mob difficulty its own ecological storytelling: Restored Hearthhome (mostly safe) → Abandoned settlement (normal hostiles) → Corrupted region (harder mobs + Shadow phenomena) → Ancient ruin (unusual enemies + Anomaly mechanics) → Legendary domain (completely different rules).

When a boss is included, it should belong to an existing system rather than being generic — e.g. an Occultism boss tied to an escaped ritual (defeating it restores an area, unlocks research, and reveals ancient-civilization lore), or a Shadow boss framed as “an ecosystem has become fundamentally wrong,” requiring investigation before the fight rather than just a fight. Status: 🟡 Candidate — strong direction, no specific boss roster locked.

11a. Titan Pokémon (new proposal — resolves the boss-content tension above)

Wesley's proposal, elegant enough that it deserves highlighting: instead of importing a whole separate boss mod (the exact thing Section 11 above argues against), turn Minecraft's own iconic bosses/mobs INTO custom Fakemon — the same technique All The Mons uses (their own changelog references “Creepyon” and “Piglichu” as real shipped custom species). This needs no new technology at all: it's the identical custom-species pipeline already fully documented in Part 1 (Blockbench model + resolver + species JSON), just themed after vanilla/modded mobs instead of Fusion results. Because each candidate is already part of the base game world rather than an imported mod's separate lore, it automatically satisfies Section 11's “what does this mean in our world?” requirement — no extra justification needed the way an Ender's Cataclysm boss would.

F.R.M. term coining: named Titan Pokémon rather than the working title “Boss Pokémon,” to avoid the term “boss” colliding with ordinary usage elsewhere (gym/faction/NPC bosses, etc.) while keeping the intended double meaning — a genuine boss encounter, and “titan” already carries the right connotation of something massive and consequential. Confirmed by Wesley with an explicit mythological rationale worth preserving: in Greek myth, the Titans weren't simply defeated — they were overthrown by a newer generation of power and then sealed away. That's precisely the two-stage mechanic below: the ancient/primal form is defeated, and what's revealed beneath it gets sealed into a Poké Ball. The name isn't just evocative, it's structurally accurate to what actually happens in the encounter.

🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): raid dens as the actual second-stage encounter chamber. Rather than the revealed Pokémon simply being caught with a flat master-ball-style trivial capture after the boss fight, the second stage repurposes (or purpose-builds) a raid-den-style structure as the actual encounter chamber — real infrastructure already sitting in M.M.I. as a confirmed candidate (Cobblemon Raid Dens Addon, type-themed den designs with automatic boss-type assignment), not a new system invented from scratch. This gives the Titan reveal genuine mechanical weight (a real battle encounter with proper stakes, naturally multiplayer-capable via existing den mechanics) rather than an anticlimactic catch after the hard part is already over.

*🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): the hard boundary between Titans and the separate Mutant tier (Part 7, Ecological Apex hierarchy) — MUTANTS NEVER BECOME CATCHABLE POKÉMON. TITANS ALWAYS DO. This is the load-bearing rule that keeps the two systems from blurring into each other: a mutant hostile (Mutant Monsters mod, M.M.I.) is a permanently-uncatchable stronger variant of an ordinary mob, while a Titan is always, without exception, a boss-to-Pokémon transformation that ends in a real catch. Any future design pass that lets a mutant become catchable, or a Titan stay permanently uncatchable, has broken this boundary and should be corrected.*

The Titan Pokémon mechanic — the two-stage encounter (locked)

The full structure, resolving what was previously an open mechanics question: Vanilla Boss Fight (the mob fought exactly as it behaves in vanilla — the Wither's shield phase, the Ender Dragon's perch phase, translating existing behavior rather than inventing new boss design from scratch) → Defeat → Resonance Collapse (the manifestation destabilizes rather than simply dying — this is the moment it stops being “just a Minecraft boss”) → Titan Pokémon Revealed (the entity beneath the manifestation is shown for what it actually was) → Second Battle (a genuine Cobblemon encounter, not vanilla combat) → Capture / Defeat / Resolution.

This retroactively explains, rather than needing a separate justification for, the rule immediately below it: the vanilla fight itself IS the preparation — you cannot skip straight to a Pokémon battle with a Titan, because the game doesn't consider you to have earned that battle until you've beaten what it was hiding behind.

- The capture rule (fused, Wesley): a Titan cannot be caught with a normal ball at any point, and the specially-prepared ball/Core (Part 8's Attunement Core / Treatment system) can ONLY be used during the second-battle capture phase — not during the vanilla boss fight, not before the Titan is Revealed. This closes off any exploit path (no throwing prepared balls at the vanilla-form fight) and gives the capture window real narrative weight: the special equipment only becomes valid once the game has actually acknowledged what you're fighting is a Pokémon.

- 🔵 Current proposal (Sept 2026, surfaced via a parallel ChatGPT exploration, genuinely new against this archive): if the Capture Phase attempt fails, the Titan does not simply vanish or reset the encounter — it escapes, fleeing back into the world as a real, persistent, rediscoverable entity rather than a dead loss or something that only exists via save-scumming. Gives failure a real consequence (the Titan is now out there somewhere, possibly warier or relocated) without being punishing in the sense of losing progress permanently — the player gets to hunt it again rather than the encounter simply ending. Not yet locked; worth deciding whether the escaped Titan relocates, changes behavior, or remains findable in roughly the same area.

- 🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): Beast Ball as a shared baseline, developed into THREE branches rather than a single retirement/replacement (refines the earlier Ball Function Reference recommendation, which only proposed a straight merge into Dimensional Ball). Beast Ball's real mechanic — poor against ordinary Pokémon, excellent against a narrow special category — becomes the reference point for three distinct Anomaly-family balls, each keyed to a different kind of displacement/transformation: DIMENSIONAL BALL for spatial displacement (Ultra Beasts), TEMPORAL BALL for temporal displacement (Paradox Pokémon, already a named candidate), and a new TITAN BALL for Titanization specifically (bosses transformed into Pokémon, Section 11a above). All three share Beast Ball's narrow-but-strong identity rather than being flat reskins of each other.

- 🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): the Titan Ball's first appearance is a discovery hook, not a crafted unlock. The player's very first Titan encounter grants a single Titan Ball as a mystery item BEFORE its purpose is explained or the Titan Ball/Titan Pokémon concept has been introduced at all — the player has to work out through play (and the eventual Capture Phase itself) that this is the one item that can actually catch what they're facing, retroactively motivating research into Titan Pokémon and Titan Balls as a real discovery arc rather than a tutorial popup. Consistent with Discovery Over Prescription.

- 🔵 Current proposal (Wesley, Sept 2026): during the Capture Phase specifically, the game could actively highlight/restrict which balls the player is shown as usable — not merely relying on invalid balls silently failing when thrown (which remains the correct fallback/safety net regardless). A real UI restriction is technically achievable — the capture-phase window already needs custom logic to gate ball validity at all (per the already-locked capture-phase rule, Section above), so the same check that currently just blocks an invalid throw could instead filter what appears selectable in whatever UI represents the Capture Phase, giving the player a genuine ‘here's what's available’ read rather than trial-and-error. Not yet designed in detail — exact UI approach (item-frame-style display, a dedicated capture-phase menu, hotbar dimming) is open.

- Investigation-gated, not just encountered — consistent with Section 11's “a boss must belong to an existing system” rule.

- The original resolution-not-just-loot idea is kept, with the trigger condition generalized: rather than requiring a kill, a defeat-or-capture-style requirement (or whichever framing fits the specific Titan) triggers the payoff — restoring the surrounding area, unlocking research, or revealing lore, per Section 11's worked examples.

Titan Pokémon's place in the taxonomy, updated now that Part 7's long-open question is resolved: Titan is a manifestation-class/subfamily of Ecological Apex Pokémon (Part 7), the same tier as Territorial, Ancient, Resonance-Saturated, Ecosystem Guardian, and Distorted/Shadow — not a standalone system sitting outside that taxonomy. What makes Titan distinct from the other subfamilies is specifically its two-stage structure: a vanilla Minecraft boss encounter as the first manifestation, with the Apex Pokémon itself revealed only after that's resolved. Alpha remains a fully separate phenotype axis, so a specific individual could in principle be, for example, an Alpha Titan (physically exceptional AND a two-stage vanilla-boss manifestation) — the axes stack independently rather than competing. Status: 🕒 Locked for the two-stage mechanic, its name, and its place as an Apex subfamily; 🟡 Candidate remaining for exact roster mechanics per Titan (Attunement Core requirements, specific payoff per candidate).

Sculk-Touched / “Wardenized” (Form-layer variant)

A separate, smaller idea from the same conversation: a rare-spawn texture/behavior variant — not a new species — for ordinary Pokémon that naturally spawn in the Deep Dark/Ancient Cities. Filed under the Form layer in the merged taxonomy (Part 10), alongside Regional forms, per Wesley's own instinct: these are normal Pokémon, just texture-swapped under specific rare spawn conditions, not a distinct Ecological/Resonance state.

Easter egg, confirmed for inclusion

Wesley is including the following as an in-pack easter egg: three Wither Skeletons walk into a Nether Fortress; one of them evolves; the other two look personally attacked, because apparently the evolution requirement was “be near two friends and a pumpkin,” and nobody told them showing up empty-handed wasn't going to cut it. (A joke about the real Wither's summoning requirement — 3 Wither Skeleton Skulls + a Soul Sand/Soil pumpkin structure.)

12\. Mod Audit Anti-Bloat Policy

Recovered via the parallel sweep as an explicit policy list, consistent with the Justified Complexity Rule (Authorities Archive): avoid generic quest spam; avoid dozens of redundant Pokémon currencies; avoid random loot-rarity inflation; avoid large quantities of unrelated structures; avoid machines that exist only to justify another machine; avoid giant weapon/armor progression unless directly justified; avoid generic RPG classes/stat systems that compete with the pack's own identity (relevant to the Skill Tree system, Part 11); avoid duplicate storage/map/economy/biome systems; prefer native NeoForge solutions when good options exist; permit a Fabric-bridge mod only when the benefit materially outweighs the compatibility cost; never claim an orphaned dependency without checking the actual installed JAR/dependency list (see Dependency Sweep, Authorities Archive). Status: 🕒 Locked — explicit policy, not situational advice.

Confirms the native-Cobblemon-over-external-mod direction already established for Alpha Pokémon (Part 10) and Pokémon riding — a separate basic riding addon was floated historically but is now superseded, since native Cobblemon riding covers the same ground without an extra dependency.

13\. IV Fusion Research Pipeline & Item Reclassification

A fully worked-through system giving Brecher's Cobblemon Fusion (confirmed adopted, Section 9's mod list) its actual place in C.E.R., rather than being sidelined for colliding with the word “Fusion.” Confirms and extends the Resonance Fusion vs. IV Fusion split from Part 9 (“what the Pokémon is” vs. “what the Pokémon is capable of”).

Stat-item reclassification

Nature Mints, Protein, Iron, Zinc, Calcium, Carbos, HP Up, and similar vanilla/Cobblemon stat items become research materials and IV Fusion inputs rather than items fed directly to a Pokémon. Progression: Natural phenomenon (a Pokémon naturally has certain traits) → Observed phenomenon (researchers discover the traits can be influenced) → Reproduced phenomenon (C.E.R. develops a controlled method) → Advanced Fusion methodology (the player gains access to it). The items don't become obsolete — they keep their recognizable identity as research materials, catalysts, consumables, loot, or inputs, just not as a direct feed-to-Pokémon shortcut.

Explicit rule, confirmed directly by Wesley: stat-changing items should be disabled for direct use on a Pokémon specifically to prevent bypassing the IV Fusion system (“I already have the candy, why not just feed it to Cyndaquil”). General principle, not a blanket ban: if an item's direct use would bypass a C.E.R. system that intentionally replaces that functionality, its vanilla direct-use behavior should be disabled or redirected — items without a competing C.E.R. system keep normal vanilla behavior.

Brecher's mechanical role

The mod's actual catalysts get a thematic reinterpretation rather than staying generic IV tools: Iron Catalyst and Gold Catalyst become part of the controlled-methodology side of the pipeline above. The Corrupted Catalyst (which deliberately takes the LOWER IV) is specifically repurposed as a research mechanic — controlled degradation / genetic study of how Pokémon populations adapt to damaged environments, tying directly to Twisted Forms (Part 3), population health, and conservation research rather than being read as simply “the bad catalyst.”

Berries, Nature Mints, and Relic Coins — a three-way thematic split

|              |                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Category** | **Theme**             | **Role**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Berries      | Life/Ecology          | Restoration catalysts, ecological samples, cultivation research, Affinity-reactive ingredients, Resonance Processing inputs — valuable for ecological properties, not just sale price                                                                             |
| Nature Mints | Biology/Individuality | Evidence that Pokémon temperament/characteristics are modifiable, interpretable biological phenomena — feeds the same research pipeline as the stat items above (“Nature Research → Behavioral/Temperamental Resonance”)                                          |
| Relic Coins  | History/Memory        | Not currency — artifacts from before the ecological collapse/reawakening, revealing lost civilizations, historical factions, old researchers, extinct ecological practices, previous restoration attempts, old Resonance technology, and Legendary/Mythical clues |

Status: 🕒 Locked — including mod adoption. The reclassification principle, the disable-direct-use rule, the Berries/Mints/Coins split, Brecher's catalyst reinterpretation, and Brecher's Cobblemon Fusion itself as the confirmed mechanical basis of the IV Fusion branch are all locked. Exact mechanics/recipes/numeric values remain 🟡 Candidate, since those were always meant for the implementation phase rather than the design phase.

14\. Bridge-Eligible Mod Principle & Loader Classification

A formal rule for when a cross-loader bridge (e.g. Forgified Fabric) is actually worth including, quoted directly since the wording itself was approved as-is: “A cross-loader bridge may be included when it enables a genuinely valuable mod or system that has no sufficiently equivalent native NeoForge implementation, provided the added compatibility burden does not outweigh the benefit.” Deliberately not decided case-by-case in advance — evaluated at the actual Mod Audit stage, not pre-judged.

Every mod candidate should carry loader as first-class metadata going forward: NeoForge, Fabric, Forge (where historically/relevantly applicable), Cross-loader/bridge-dependent, or Unknown/requires verification — with loader-specific subsections planned for the eventual full Mod Candidate list, alongside the overall candidate view. Status: 🕒 Locked — explicit stated principle.

Cobblemon Feature Audit — structure confirmed and expanded

Refines Part 10's note that a full Cobblemon Feature Audit is planned but not yet performed. Confirmed evaluation structure for that audit, expanded beyond the original version: Vanilla purpose → C.E.R. potential → Cross-mod potential → Progression relevance → Research relevance → Affinity relevance → Reward potential → Loot-table potential → Other applications → Status. The “other applications” catch-all is deliberate — an item with almost no mechanical significance in vanilla Cobblemon could still be a perfect rare archaeological loot item, quest reward, research sample, crafting component, or Resonance Selection/Memory Phenomenon manifestation.

Reconstruction status

Remaining explicitly-flagged open items across all four parts: the Noble Pokémon/Domain relationship (flagged historical/unclear per your review, later expanded in Part 6/7), the Resonance Heart (material) vs. Resonance Hearts (player progression) naming overlap (resolved — material renamed to Resonance Core, see Part 3), the Affinity Observatory → Restoration Observatory naming resolution (resolved — confirmed as Restoration Observatory, a circular ruin with 18 sockets), and the exact Pokémon→Virtue Pool mapping (unresolved in the source material itself). The JavaScript example document has not yet been separately reviewed — recommend a short follow-up pass to confirm its code aligns with what's documented here, once you've had a chance to review Parts 1–4.*

Titan Battle Transition Mechanics (Sept 2026, new)

LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): the boss-to-Pokemon transition must be a single continuous atomic event with no in-between idle state — explicitly rejected: 'boss dies, time passes, player has to manually start the battle or it just sits there.' Instead: Titan boss HP reaches 0 → the boss immediately enters an invulnerable TRANSITION state (cannot be damaged, cannot despawn, cannot be interacted with, drops no normal boss loot, prevents duplicate-kill/duplicate-Titan exploits) → the same entity visibly transforms into its Titan Pokemon form (not a delete-and-respawn swap) → the Pokemon battle initializes immediately, same event, no gap. The player should see one creature with two manifestations, not two separate encounters stitched together.

Pokemon selection during the transition uses an interactive 6-spoke radial wheel (Tool Belt / Iron's Spells-style), not a conventional list menu and not a forced first-slot send-out. Each spoke shows the Pokemon's icon, name, level, and HP/status; hovering enlarges/highlights it; center displays details for the currently hovered entry. Default behavior waits for player selection (this is the intended experience, not a timeout-driven default); an automatic first-eligible-Pokemon fallback exists only as a safety net against input/UI failure, not as the normal flow. Selection triggers the battle immediately — the wheel is treated as a reusable Titan Encounter Controller component, not a one-off UI, with the deliberate design goal that it could later serve other forced-battle or partner-selection contexts.

Reward timing: the Minecraft boss phase itself grants little to nothing (at most a small material/visual token); the ACTUAL Titan reward (loot, research progress, advancement, quest completion, Affinity/Resonance consequences) fires only on winning the Pokemon battle phase, making the Pokemon battle the true conclusion of the encounter rather than a bonus tacked onto an already-resolved fight.

Losing the Pokemon battle phase does NOT kill/delete the Titan — it retreats/reverts rather than dying, preserving the ability to re-attempt the encounter under whatever cooldown/respawn rules eventually get set. This directly reuses the escaped-Titan-on-capture-failure design pattern already locked elsewhere in this Part, extended here to cover battle-phase loss specifically, not just capture-phase failure.

*🔵 Current proposal, not fully locked: a three-state Titan lifecycle distinct from a simple respawn timer — MANIFESTED (a living Titan currently exists and can be fought), DORMANT (the manifestation has destabilized and reverted to its underlying phenomenon/domain after being left unengaged too long), and the underlying source/Remnant (persists even when no living Titan is currently manifested, explaining why a Titan can reappear later without being treated as an ordinary respawning boss). Ties conceptually to the Draconic Evolution Ender Dragon/Chaos Guardian Titan-candidate brainstorm below.*

Draconic Evolution Titan Candidates & Chaos Shard Integration (Sept 2026, brainstorm, not locked)

🔵 Genuinely speculative, flagged explicitly by Wesley as spur-of-the-moment: the Ender Dragon and Draconic Evolution's Chaos Guardian as two additional Titan candidates, each representing a different phenomenon rather than two more generic bosses. Ender Dragon proposed as a Dragon/End Titan — major Dragon Resonance, tied to End-domain restoration/investigation. Chaos Guardian proposed as a Chaos/Corruption-adjacent Titan representing extreme Resonance instability specifically — explicitly NOT proposed as requiring a 19th 'Chaos Affinity'; the cleaner reading kept is that the 18 Affinities describe elemental/ecological relationships, Corruption describes degradation/inversion (already locked elsewhere), and Chaos would describe extreme concentration/instability, with Dragon Affinity happening to interact unusually well with that state rather than being synonymous with it.

*Chaos Shards (Draconic Evolution) proposed as a manifestation of unstable/corrupted Resonance rather than literal Dragon-type crafting material — Dragon Affinity could be what a shard resonates toward when exposed under stable conditions, while exposure under corrupted conditions could instead yield a Corrupted Chaos Shard feeding Shadow research specifically. Both the Titan candidates and the Chaos Shard integration remain pure brainstorm — worth a full audit of Draconic Evolution for genuine Affinity-interaction hooks before anything here gets promoted past candidate status.*

## C. Master Archive Part 5

Cobblemon: Ecological Resonance

Master Archive — Part 5: Technical Implementation Notes

*Compiled by Claude, September 2026. Source: the “Cobblemon EcoRe JavaScript example” document. That document is mostly iterative KubeJS code drafts — the same two scripts (a Personal Affinity slot calculator and a slot-unlock blueprint) reworked roughly six times with small refinements, plus scattered one-off scripts for quest gating, starter selection, and catch-event hooks. Rather than reproducing draft code in a design archive, this note preserves the concrete design decisions the code reveals — the source document itself remains the implementation reference. Everything below is 🕒 Locked in the sense that it's concrete, tested-in-script logic rather than an open brainstorm, though none of it has been confirmed as actually built/running in the modpack yet.*

1\. Personal Affinity Slot Count — Resolved to 6

*Part 1 left the active-affinity capacity as “4–6 depending on progression, exact numbers tunable.” The implementation scripts confirm the endgame number as exactly 6, unlocked via a specific gate sequence rather than a smooth curve. Refinement recovered via the parallel full-sweep pass: slot assignment is organic, not manually locked — the script automatically sorts the player's 18 Affinity scores and assigns the highest-ranking ones to however many slots are currently unlocked. If a lower-active Affinity (e.g. Ghost) eventually overtakes a currently-active one (e.g. Water), Ghost automatically claims the higher slot rather than the player needing to manually swap. Status: 🟡 Candidate — the parallel sweep flags this specific point as still unresolved: whether slot assignment should be fully automatic, fully manual, or a hybrid (automatic ranking with a manual override) has not been decided. Preserve as an open question rather than assuming full automation is final.*

The gate sequence itself:

- Slot 1: assigned automatically at character creation to the starter's element (example given: choosing Charmander auto-assigns Slot 1 to Fire at Personal Affinity 25).

- Slots 2–4: unlocked through ordinary progression (mechanism not fully specified in the surviving script fragments).

- Slot 5 (“The Legendary Chosen One”): unlocked by reaching Personal Affinity 100 on any one type, OR capturing a Legendary/Mythical Pokémon — requires crafting a Legendary Attunement Core (Resonance Shards + a Nether Star + a Diamond Block) and right-clicking it; the item refuses to consume and tells the player what they're missing if requirements aren't met yet.

- Slot 6 (“Cosmic Convergence”): unlocked by clearing the modpack's endgame boss / main content (a persistent “pack_cleared” flag), via a Cosmic Nexus Key (Cosmic Lens + Netherite Ingot + Nether Star). Explicitly designed as a New Game Plus trigger.

2\. Replay Mode (New Game Plus)

A previously undocumented system: completing the pack once (the same “pack_cleared” flag that unlocks Slot 6) enables a Replay Mode for future save files. On a Replay Mode save, choosing a starter grants an upgraded starting loadout beyond the normal kit — the given example: choosing a Dragon-type starter on a cleared-pack file grants the standard starting gear plus custom Dragon-attuned Resonance Balls, extra Ender Pearls, and an instant +25 starting Personal Dragon Affinity, letting a replaying player field-test a build immediately rather than regrinding from zero. This directly implements the Replayability goal from Part 4 (different playthroughs should diverge) as a concrete NG+ mechanic rather than just varied starting conditions.

Confirmed by the parallel full-sweep pass: the completion flag is persistent and stored outside the individual world (so it survives world deletion/recreation), and the plan discussed was to bypass/replace the native starter-selection screen via KubeJS so a Replay Mode save can expose secret/challenge starters unavailable on a first playthrough, on top of the bonus loadout above. Status: 🟢 Strong reconstruction — confirmed as a real designed system across two independent sweeps; exact bonus loadouts per element and the secret-starter roster are not fully specified.

3\. Resonance/Affinity Ball Implementation — the Strange Ball Hijack

A concrete technical path was worked out for implementing the 18 Resonance/Affinity Balls (referenced only conceptually in Part 3's material families) without writing a full Java addon: Cobblemon's Strange Ball already has a fully-coded 3D model, inventory texture, thrown-entity state, and capture animation, and Cobblemon falls back to rendering it whenever it encounters a Poké Ball variant it can't otherwise resolve. The proposed approach hijacks this via resource packs (distinct visuals per Affinity) and data packs (distinct recipes per Affinity) layered on top of the single underlying Strange Ball item, avoiding custom Java code for the visual/recipe layer. Status: ⚪ Historical/superseded — this was the original plan; see the project-direction update further down this section for the current preferred approach.

4\. Custom Poké Ball / Fakemon Implementation Options

This directly addresses the “Fakemon implementation” item on Part 4's design backlog, specifically for anything needing genuinely custom Poké Ball behavior (not just reskinning). Cobblemon's Poké Ball entities/items are hardcoded, so a purely data-pack-only approach cannot create new custom capture-logic behavior; three implementation paths were laid out:

- KubeJS approach (recommended as easiest for a modpack, not a standalone mod): register the custom item via a KubeJS startup script, then intercept Cobblemon's capture events server-side to apply custom catch-rate math (e.g. weather or status-condition modifiers) without writing Java.

- Lightweight NeoForge addon: register the item through Cobblemon's own API classes as a true PokeBallItem subclass, overriding the catch-calculation method or hooking Cobblemon's PreCaptureEvent/CaptureCalculationEvent directly — cleaner integration, more setup work.

- Piggyback on an existing framework: the Modular Poké Balls mod was identified as a possible no-code backend, letting new ball logic be defined via data packs against its predefined catch-power “cores” rather than building capture logic from scratch.

Status: 🟡 Candidate set of implementation paths; no final choice was locked in.

Alternative path: extend the apricorn → ball crafting chain (AllTheMons precedent)

A second real-world approach, found by researching the All the Mons modpack (ATMons — All the Mods 10 + Cobblemon, 1.9M+ downloads) rather than from the original transcripts. Instead of hijacking the Strange Ball fallback or building fully custom PokeBallItem classes, ATMons' own coremod extends Cobblemon's existing native apricorn-tree-→-ball crafting pipeline: it adds new apricorn tree variants tied to the pack's own tech-tier materials (AllTheModium, Vibranium, Unobtainium, Soul Lava), each producing a themed custom ball through that same existing crafting chain, via a small dedicated NeoForge coremod rather than a parallel ball system built from scratch.

Applied to C.E.R., the equivalent would be: 18 new apricorn tree variants (or a smaller grouped set), each tied to a Type Gem/Affinity Essence input instead of a tech material, each yielding that Affinity's themed Resonance/Affinity Ball — plugging directly into a system Cobblemon already fully supports, rather than working around the Strange Ball's fallback rendering. This is a genuine alternative to the Strange Ball hijack from Section 3, not a replacement for it — which path to take is intentionally left open until implementation actually begins on the ball system. Status: 🟡 Candidate — proven at scale in a comparable pack, not yet chosen over the other option.

Project direction update: Strange Ball retexture → Modular Poké Balls as the base

Correction/update from Wesley, not a third AllTheMons technique: the project's own plan for the Resonance/Affinity Ball system has shifted. The original approach was the Strange Ball hijack in Section 3 (retexture the Strange Ball via resource/data packs, then layer custom implementation on top). The current direction is to potentially use the Modular Poké Balls mod (Section 4's Option 3) as the actual base framework instead — building C.E.R.'s own ball designs into Modular Poké Balls' predefined catch-power "cores" system rather than retexturing the Strange Ball fallback. Framed as "potentially," not yet fully locked in.

Status: the Strange Ball hijack (Section 3) is being held in reserve rather than treated as dead — Wesley's own framing, per his direct input: it was his first idea before he knew the other paths existed, and he wants it kept as a last-resort fallback if the other two don't pan out, not discarded outright. Downgraded from 🟡 Candidate to ⚪ Historical/superseded still applies for “not the current direction,” but read that status as “banked, not buried.”

Modular Poké Balls as base is now Wesley's stronger lean, with explicit reasoning worth preserving: most of the underlying system is already built (so it doubles as a fast proof-of-concept before deciding whether a standalone addon is worth it), and critically, it hands the player genuine creative agency over ball-making — “I wonder what this, this, and this will make” rather than “they made the ball do X, that's cool,” which fits the project's Research/Discovery theming (D.O.P.) far better than a purely designer-authored ball roster. The apricorn-crafting-chain path and the Section 4 KubeJS/NeoForge options remain open alternatives, not eliminated.

Noted want, not yet a design: Wesley would like to find a way to include a Dark Ball (from the anime) somewhere in this system — flagged here for whenever ball implementation actually starts.

5\. Custom Species Fusion — Full Worked Example (Solara)

A second technical conversation (provided separately by Wesley, possibly from a different ChatGPT account/session — not certain it was already in pt1–pt3) confirms and extends the Fusion pipeline from Part 1 with a complete worked example. Confirmed: Poke Fusion's own documented recipe format uses speciesId for both inputs and the result, and does not need to understand or generate a model itself — it only needs a valid target species ID to exist somewhere in Cobblemon's species system.

Worked example given: Charizard + Lucario → a new custom species called Solara (ecoresonance:solara, Fire/Steel). The addon file structure laid out: a data/cobblemon/species/custom/solara.json (gameplay data — types, abilities, base stats, catch rate, egg groups, etc.) plus a resource-side set under assets/cobblemon/bedrock/pokemon/ — a Blockbench model (models/solara/solara.geo.json), a poser (posers/solara.json, binding idle/walk/battle/cry/faint animations), a resolver (resolvers/solara/0_solara_base.json, the file that actually links the species ID to its model/texture/poser), textures (including a shiny variant), and a lang file entry for name/Pokédex description. The Poke Fusion recipe itself then only needs three lines: the two input speciesIds and the result speciesId — confirming the pipeline diagram in Part 1.

A recommended dedicated namespace convention was reconfirmed: ecoresonance:\<name\> (e.g. ecoresonance:solara, ecoresonance:shadow_dragon, ecoresonance:verdant_eevee) to avoid colliding with Cobblemon's own species IDs and to let Shadow/Fusion/restored-ancient/Affinity-specific Pokémon coexist cleanly. Recommended practical next step, worth preserving as advice for whenever implementation actually starts: build one single Charizard+Lucario→Solara prototype end-to-end first (confirm it spawns with its custom model) before building out the rest of the Fusion roster, and lock down the exact Minecraft/Cobblemon/Poke Fusion versions being targeted before writing the addon, since folder structure and JSON schemas have changed across Cobblemon versions (older addons pre-1.4 used a different resolver folder convention). Status: 🕒 Locked — this is a confirmed-workable technical pipeline, checked directly against current Poke Fusion/Cobblemon documentation rather than assumed.

Cobblemon's aspect/resolver system was also reconfirmed as the mechanism for giving one fused species further progression states without needing separate species entries — e.g. a single ecoresonance:solara could carry normal / shadow / stellar / perfected / unstable / awakened visual aspects, meaning a Fusion result doesn't have to be a dead end (Charizard + Lucario → Solara → Fire Affinity Resonance achieved → Awakened Solara → Shadow Solara → Perfect Resonance Solara, all still one underlying species handled by Cobblemon's normal rendering).

6\. Assigning Affinity to an Individual Pokémon

Confirmed design decision: Affinity should be an individual Pokémon property, not a species-level or form-level property — i.e. two wild Pikachu can have different Affinities from each other (e.g. one Storm-affinity, one Verdant-affinity), the same way two individual Pokémon can have different natures or IVs today. This was an explicit choice given how deeply Affinity was already planned to interact with Resonance, Shadow, Fusion, Fakemon, factions, and Dynamic Spawning — locking Affinity to species or form would have been simpler but much less flexible.

Explicit caution: don't just add an arbitrary “affinity” field directly to Cobblemon's species JSON — Cobblemon's species schema doesn't natively support it, so an unrecognized field would not automatically become a functioning mechanic. Three real implementation approaches were laid out:

|                          |                                                                                                                  |                         |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| **Approach**             | **Best for**                                                                                                     | **Relative difficulty** |
| Aspect-based             | Different Pokémon/forms having different Affinities (form-level granularity)                                     | Low                     |
| Custom data/component    | Every individual Pokémon having its own Affinity (individual-level granularity — the recommended approach above) | Medium                  |
| Dedicated mod/API system | Full Resonance mechanics — progression, abilities, reactions built on top of Affinity                            | High                    |

Status: 🕒 Locked for “Affinity is per-individual-Pokémon, implemented via custom data/component, not a raw species-JSON field”; 🟡 Candidate for the exact component schema, which wasn't specified further pending confirmation of the target Cobblemon version.

Claude's technical opinion, per Wesley's request

Asked directly whether this approach holds up: yes, this is the right call, for the reason the original answer gave — Cobblemon Pokémon already carry persistent per-individual data (IVs, EVs, nature, ability, etc.), so a custom data component attached the same way is the idiomatic, low-friction approach rather than a workaround. Two things worth adding on top of what was already said:

- Concretely, this should use NeoForge's Data Attachment API (the modern standard for exactly this kind of per-instance custom data, introduced to replace the older, more boilerplate-heavy Capability pattern) rather than a bespoke Capability implementation — less code, and it's what current Cobblemon addons generally reach for first.

- The real risk isn't the initial assignment logic, it's persistence through everything Cobblemon does to a Pokémon afterward — PC storage, trading, dimension changes, server restarts. That's historically where these systems quietly break. Worth a small end-to-end prototype early (assign an Affinity, then deliberately trade/PC-store/reload and confirm it survives) before building anything else on top of the assumption that it will.

Status: 🔵 Current proposal — Claude's own technical opinion, offered as requested, not a recovered decision.

7\. Attunement Cores (historical name: Resonance Cores)

Newly surfaced by Wesley via a separate ChatGPT conversation — not previously in the archives. This is the original, more developed meaning of “Resonance Core,” distinct from the Part 3 materials-table entry now renamed Resonance Nexus (see that entry's note for the naming history).

Concept: Type Gems were always meant to be more than ordinary crafting materials — they represent condensed, type-specific Resonance/Affinity. Attunement Cores are the next refinement step: Fire Type Gem → Fire Attunement Core, Water Type Gem → Water Attunement Core, Ghost Type Gem → Ghost Attunement Core, and so on across all 18 Affinities. Their primary intended use is specialized Poké Ball construction — giving a ball real type-specific properties instead of a generic “5× catch rate” modifier:

- Better compatibility with Pokémon of that Affinity

- Improved capture behavior

- Increased research value

- Interaction with the player's Personal/Trainer Affinity

- Environmental bonuses

- Special behavior around anomalies or particular ecosystems

Worked examples given: a Fire Attunement Core granting advantages around Fire Pokémon and high-temperature environments; a Ghost Attunement Core interacting with Ghost Pokémon, Occultism, Shadow phenomena, haunted structures, and death-related discoveries — directly relevant to the ball-system paths in Section 6 above, since this is likely the actual per-type specialization layer any of those three ball-implementation paths would ultimately use.

Naming history: originally called Resonance Core(s). Renamed to Attunement Core specifically because “Resonance Core” inside a “Resonance Ball” read as muddy — the established distinction became Core = the physical capture-power component, Attunement Core = the type/Affinity specialization component, Resonance Ball = the finished, Affinity-aligned ball configuration/philosophy that can contribute to World Affinity. Status: 🟢 Strong reconstruction for the core concept and the historical→current naming; 🟡 Candidate for exact mechanical properties and values, which were illustrative rather than finalized.

*🕒 RESOLVED (Sept 2026, confirmed via the actual KubeJS implementation script): the Legendary Attunement Core is a DIFFERENT item from this ball-component Attunement Core family — a naming collision, not a shared-family member. The Legendary Attunement Core is specifically a Personal Affinity Slot 5 unlock consumable (Resonance Shards + Nether Star + Diamond Block, requires one Affinity at Level 100), unrelated to Modular Ball type-specialization. Same shape as the already-resolved Resonance Heart/Resonance Hearts collision — recommend renaming the Slot 5 item (e.g. to 'Legendary Soul Core' or similar, exact name not locked) to stop the two from sharing a name going forward, now that implementation is approaching and this kind of collision gets more expensive to untangle later.*
