## C. Master Archive Part 7

Cobblemon: Ecological Resonance

Master Archive — Part 7: New Design Proposals (Domains & Nobles)

*Compiled by Claude, September 2026, under Free Reign Mode. Unlike Parts 1–6, this part is NOT reconstructed from the transcripts — it's original design work, explicitly invited by Wesley to fill two gaps that were never fully developed in the source material: the unfinished Legendary Domains (Light, Night, Creation, Balance) and the Noble Pokémon ↔ Legendary Domain relationship. Every entry here is 🔵 Current proposal, Claude-originated, offered as a starting point for discussion — not a recovered decision. Treat this part as the most negotiable document in the whole archive.*

1\. The Light Domain (Solgaleo)

Solgaleo holds Fundamental Light/Solar Authority. Before recognition: solar-dependent tech caps out at a low ceiling no matter how it's upgraded (solar generators, light-based crafting, anything drawing on Ars Nouveau's or Create's light-adjacent mechanics), and certain crystal/prism structures in the world sit visibly dormant — present, inert, waiting. After recognition: DOMAIN UNLOCKED: LIGHT — solar infrastructure uncaps, light-based restoration tech becomes available (accelerated growth under artificial daylight, light-purification of corrupted zones), and dormant prism structures activate.

Necrozma sits as a specialized authority within Light rather than a separate domain — Consumed/Overcharged Light, governing unstable or weaponized light energy (dangerous, high-risk/high-reward tech: overcharge mechanics, prism-based weapons or amplifiers) as a deliberately riskier counterpart to Solgaleo's stable, foundational authority. Mirrors the Dialga/Celebi and Palkia/Hoopa broad-vs-specialized pattern already established for Time and Space in Part 2.

2\. The Night/Dreams Domain (Lunala)

A structural fix as much as a new domain: Part 2 already placed Darkrai (Dreams/Nightmare) and Cresselia (Dreams/Moon, protective dreams) as floating specialized authorities with no fundamental holder above them. Lunala fills that gap naturally — Fundamental Night/Dream Authority, unifying what was already there rather than competing with it.

|             |                                |                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|-------------|--------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Pokémon** | **Authority**                  | **Governs**                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Lunala      | Fundamental Night/Dream        | Night-cycle mechanics, dream-space travel (a lightweight Ultra-Wormhole-style short-range teleport through dreams rather than Palkia's Space), moonlit-only content and structures |
| Darkrai     | Nightmare (specialized)        | Unconscious/sleep manipulation, nightmare-based hazards and rewards — unchanged from Part 2, now properly placed under a fundamental authority                                     |
| Cresselia   | Protective Dream (specialized) | Dream protection, positive dream mechanics, countering Darkrai's effects — unchanged from Part 2, now properly placed                                                              |

Before Lunala: night in C.E.R. is mechanically inert beyond normal darkness — no moonlit encounters, no dream-space anything, Darkrai/Cresselia content (however implemented) exists but doesn't connect to anything larger. After Lunala: DOMAIN UNLOCKED: NIGHT — the world's night cycle becomes an active second layer of play rather than just “when it's dark outside.”

3\. The Creation Domain (Arceus)

Deliberately built to tie back into C.O.C. (Creation Over Crafting) rather than functioning like a normal domain gate. Arceus doesn't unlock a tech tree — it unlocks a capability: the authority to define new stable outcomes within systems that already exist, rather than only using outcomes the world/player has already discovered.

Concretely: before Arceus, Resonance Processing (Part 6), Resonance Synthesis/Fusion (Part 2), and Twisted-to-official transitions (Part 3) all operate on recipes and rules the player discovers, not ones they invent. After Arceus recognition, the player gains access to a capstone system — working title Authored Resonance — letting them propose and stabilize a genuinely new Fusion pairing, a new Resonance Processing recipe, or a new stable material variant that didn't previously exist in the world, subject to whatever balance/cost gating makes sense at implementation time. This is explicitly meant as the mechanical payoff for C.O.C. as a philosophy: the ultimate creation authority is earned, not crafted, and its price is understanding everything beneath it first.

This also gives Arceus a genuinely distinct identity from every other Legendary rather than just being “the strongest one” — its domain isn't a resource or a technology, it's authorship itself.

4\. The Balance Domain (Zygarde)

This domain has a direct hook already sitting in Part 1: the hidden World Balance value (how unevenly the 18 World Affinities are distributed), explicitly floated as the true late-game objective instead of simply maxing all 18 to 100, tied to worldbuilding about why the ancient civilization removed Pokémon in the first place. Zygarde is the natural authority to gate that system.

Before Zygarde: World Balance exists and quietly affects the world (per Part 1) but is invisible to the player — no readout, no way to act on it directly, only individual Affinity numbers are visible. After Zygarde recognition: DOMAIN UNLOCKED: BALANCE — a Balance readout appears in the Restoration Observatory, and new tools become available to deliberately redistribute Affinity investment toward balance rather than toward maxing favorite types (e.g. a Redistribution ritual/device that trades surplus Affinity in an over-invested type for a boost to an under-invested one, at a meaningful cost).

Zygarde's own in-game gimmick (10% → Complete Forme) maps naturally onto this unlock: encountering Zygarde in its lesser Formes could be the “signs” stage of the Legendary-recognition flow from Part 2, with Complete Forme only appearing once the player has demonstrated enough actual balance (not just total Affinity) across their World Affinity spread — making Zygarde's transformation a genuine reflection of the player's ecological choices rather than a scripted cutscene.

5\. Nobles ↔ Legendary Domains — A Proposed Synthesis

Update: Wesley separately verified this section with his own research after this part's first draft, and recovered real confirmed material — the synthesis below is being kept largely intact since it's compatible with what came back, but the recovered facts are now folded in and marked as such rather than presented as pure proposal.

Recovered: the spawn-rarity hierarchy

Nobles sat in an actual tiered hierarchy, recovered directly: Normal Pokémon → Rare Pokémon → Pseudo/very rare species → Noble Pokémon → Legendary Pokémon. Nobles required very high Affinity plus a special event; Legendaries required extremely high Affinity plus world conditions plus a dedicated quest/event — a real, meaningful gap between the two tiers, not a synonym relationship. Status: 🟢 Strong reconstruction.

Recovered: Alpha vs. Apex vs. Noble are three different distinctions

The archive already separately established Alpha as a biological/physical phenotype (an individual specimen being physically exceptional — see Part 1) and Apex as ecological significance, with Noble apparently sitting in similar territory to Apex but recovered as its own distinct concept. These three can stack rather than being mutually exclusive — a Noble Ninetales (ecologically significant guardian) is different from an Alpha Ninetales (physically exceptional specimen), and a Noble Alpha Ninetales (both at once) is explicitly supported by the architecture's general willingness to let significance layers intersect. Status: 🟢 Strong reconstruction for Alpha vs. Noble being distinct; ❓ the precise Apex/Noble boundary specifically wasn't fully resolved even in the recovery pass — flagged rather than asserted.

RESOLVED: Ecological Apex Pokémon is the umbrella (Wesley, Sept 2026)

Locked, finally answering the question that sat open above for most of this reconstruction: Ecological Apex Pokémon IS the umbrella classification — an individual Pokémon's ecological significance, expressed through one or more named origins/subfamilies rather than a flat list of unrelated “special boss” concepts. Confirmed subfamilies: Territorial, Ancient, Resonance-Saturated, Ecosystem Guardian, Distorted/Twisted, Shadow, and — the specific trigger for finally resolving this — Titan Pokémon (Part 4, Section 11a), whose two-stage vanilla-boss-then-Pokémon-battle mechanic is now locked as one Apex manifestation-class among several, not a standalone system.

This supersedes the “separate but stackable, not unified” leaning noted below — that evidence isn't wrong, it's just describing a different layer. Alpha remains its own phenotype axis, entirely separate from Apex (Alpha ≠ Apex was always correct and stays correct). What changes is that Apex's various origins (Territorial/Ancient/Resonance-Saturated/Guardian/Distorted/Shadow/Titan) are now confirmed to sit UNDER the Apex umbrella as named subfamilies, rather than being independent concepts that merely happen to co-occur with Apex. A Pokémon can still be, for example, a Resonance-Saturated Alpha Apex — Alpha (phenotype) + Apex (ecological significance, expressed via its Resonance-Saturated origin) — the stacking behavior described below remains accurate, it's just now understood as “which Apex subfamily, plus which separate phenotype/condition axes,” not “six unrelated labels.”

Historical note, preserved rather than deleted per the Archive Preservation Principle:

*An unresolved question sitting in the transcripts for most of this reconstruction, worth preserving as the record of how this got settled: whether “Ecological Apex Pokémon” should replace “boss Pokémon” wholesale as a single unifying category, covering candidates like ancient Alpha, territorial apex predator, unusually old Pokémon, Resonance-saturated specimen, ecosystem guardian, Twisted alpha, and Shadow aberrant specimen — or whether these should stay as separate, distinct concepts. The original question, never answered for a long time: “how do they differ? Right now it just seems like they are all just 'special boss' Pokémon — can they be integrated as one, or rather, should they be?”*

*New evidence that once leaned toward “separate but stackable” rather than “unify into one category”: a sweep on Affinity Exposure (Part 9) confirmed Resonance-Saturated as its own trait arising specifically from Affinity Saturation, explicitly compatible with combinations like “Resonance-Saturated Alpha” or “Twisted Alpha” or “Territorial Apex” — with an explicit caution that the player shouldn't see six simultaneous labels stacked on one Pokémon at once, and the key framing that Exposure is a cause/process, while Alpha/Apex/Twisted/Shadow/etc. are resulting classifications from it. That evidence is preserved above as still relevant to how subfamilies and phenotype axes interact — it just no longer argues against the umbrella itself.*

Apex Encounter-Tier Hierarchy (graduated from Supplemental Archive)

Now that the umbrella question above is resolved, this proposal — previously held in Supplemental Archive's Provisional Thoughts pending exactly this resolution — has a real home: a content hierarchy for how elaborate an Apex encounter should be, so “Apex” doesn't collapse into one uniform difficulty spike. Exceptional Pokémon (a normal encounter, no special structure) → Apex Pokémon (a special but single-stage encounter) → Major Apex (a full boss-to-Pokémon two-stage encounter — this is where Titan Pokémon, Part 4 Section 11a, sits) → Guardian Apex (an environmental trial leading to recognition, potentially with no conventional battle at all, matching Part 12's principle that an Ecosystem Guardian may be better restored/recognized than fought) → Story Apex (a full multi-stage event, the rarest tier) → Legendary (out of scope for this hierarchy entirely — governed by the separate, already-locked Domain/Recognition architecture, Part 2/9).

🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): the hostile-mob taxonomy sitting below this whole Apex hierarchy

Three tiers, deliberately distinct rather than one blurred spectrum, resolving a real design question about how vanilla/modded hostile mobs relate to Cobblemon's Pokémon population without either inventing lore for every single mob or importing a whole separate monster system: (1) ORDINARY HOSTILES — regular vanilla mobs, density gated by World Affinity using the exact same mechanism already driving the Twisted-to-official Pokémon population shift (Part 3, Section 2) — no individual lore needed, their prevalence alone tells the restoration story. (2) MUTANTS — any ordinary hostile, given sustained exposure to the right Resonance/Affinity conditions, has a chance to transform into a stronger variant (mechanical/visual foundation: Mutant Monsters, M.M.I.) — permanently uncatchable, never becomes a Pokémon, exists purely as discovery-driven environmental danger. (3) TITANS — the existing Major Apex tier above (Part 4, Section 11a) — always resolves into a genuine catch via the boss-to-Pokémon two-stage encounter.

The hard rule that keeps tiers 2 and 3 from blurring into each other, worth restating here since it governs this whole hierarchy: MUTANTS NEVER BECOME CATCHABLE POKÉMON. TITANS ALWAYS DO. Mutants answer ‘did this get stronger’; Titans answer ‘was this something else all along.’ Different questions, which is exactly what lets both exist without competing for the same narrative space.

*Cosmological grounding, tying this into the already-locked backstory (Part 2): if C.E.R. is explicitly set in the Pokémon multiverse, hostile mobs are not imports from the player's origin world — they're native to the same Pokémon War/catastrophe that produced the Sundering itself, a conflict between righteous and hostile Pokémon (Legends included) that damaged the Domains and is why they need healing in the first place. This also explains, as a side effect, why every other trainer and NPC in the world already understands Pokémon while the player and their companions are learning from scratch — the player's people are the outsiders here, not the world's wildlife.*

This gives every Apex subfamily (Territorial/Ancient/Resonance-Saturated/Guardian/Distorted/Shadow/Titan) a way to express itself at different intensities rather than each subfamily needing its own separate difficulty system. Status: 🟡 Candidate — a strong, now-unblocked proposal, not yet locked in its own right.

Explicitly NOT recovered: a direct Noble→Domain Authority link

Important honesty check from the recovery itself: no preserved source statement says “Nobles grant Domain Authority” or otherwise directly mechanically links the two systems. What's recovered is that the two systems were independently developing into similar philosophical territory at around the same time, without an explicit bridge ever being written down. That's exactly the gap the proposal below tries to fill — it remains a proposal, not a recovery, even after this round of checking.

The proposed synthesis (unchanged in substance, now better-grounded)

Proposed distinction: Nobles and Legendaries are different tiers of the same underlying idea, not competitors for the same narrative role.

|                                 |                                                                                                                       |                                                                                                                                            |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|                                 | **Nobles**                                                                                                            | **Legendaries (Domain holders)**                                                                                                           |
| Scope                           | Local/regional — tied to a specific biome or area's World Affinity                                                    | Cosmic/global — tied to a whole Domain of reality                                                                                          |
| Identity                        | Unnamed or loosely-named — “the spirit of this restored place,” potentially several per type across different regions | Individually named, unique, one per Aspect within a Domain (per Part 2's Domain/Aspect/Authority structure)                                |
| Trigger                         | A single region's Affinity crossing a high local threshold (per Part 1's original 750/900/1000 tiers)                 | World Affinity plus Personal Affinity plus Hearts plus Virtues plus location/research/events (per Part 2's eligibility → recognition flow) |
| What defeating/appeasing grants | Local affinity stabilization for that region only (per Part 1's original concept, unchanged)                          | Full Domain Authority — world-changing, permanent, affects everyone (per Part 2)                                                           |

Under this framing, meeting a Noble becomes the earlier, smaller-scale version of the exact same emotional beat as meeting a Legendary — “the world is thanking you for restoring it, locally” before the much bigger “the world is fundamentally changing because of what you did, globally.” A player might meet several Nobles across different regions over the course of a playthrough before ever encountering their first true Domain-holding Legendary, which would also help solve the pacing problem of Legendaries otherwise being purely late-game events — Nobles give the Legendary-adjacent fantasy an early- and mid-game presence too.

This would also finally explain why Nobles were floated so early in the original brainstorming and then never returned to: they may simply have been the right idea at the wrong layer of abstraction — proposed before the Domain system existed to give them a place underneath. Status: 🔵 Current proposal — this is new synthesis work, explicitly offered for you to accept, modify, or discard. If anything about the original Noble concept comes back to you, it slots in as evidence either for or against this framing rather than needing to overturn it entirely.

## C. Master Archive Part 8

Cobblemon: Ecological Resonance

Master Archive — Part 8: The Custom Poké Ball / Modular Ball System

*Compiled by Claude, September 2026, under Free Reign Mode. Newly recovered by Wesley via a separate ChatGPT research pass — the richest single piece of material in the project so far, covering the full custom ball architecture: components, capture cores, Attunement Cores, the Resonance/Affinity Ball terminology (which went through three historical versions — preserved honestly below rather than picking one and pretending it was always settled), Treatments, Anomaly Balls, faction integration, Occupied Pokéballs, and the ball's role in Pokémon history. This confirms and substantially deepens the ball-system content in Part 5 rather than replacing it — cross-references noted throughout.*

1\. Core Philosophy: “No Best Ball”

Explicit governing principle: No Best Ball. Only the best ball for this situation. Deliberately contrasted with the conventional Poké Ball → Great Ball → Ultra Ball obsolescence ladder — balls with comparable capture power should have different situational purposes instead. Intended player mindset progression: “I need a ball” → “I need the right ball” → “I need to design the right ball.” Status: 🕒 Locked — stated as an explicit design rule, not a brainstorm.

2\. Modular Ball Architecture

A ball is assembled from interchangeable components. The component list evolved during discussion (preserved below in its most detailed recovered form), but the modular-construction concept itself stayed consistent throughout:

|                 |                                 |
|-----------------|---------------------------------|
| **Component**   | **Role**                        |
| Lid             | Ball identity / visual language |
| Colors          | Personal expression             |
| Core            | Capture strength                |
| Attunement Core | Type/ecological alignment       |
| Treatment       | Functional specialization       |
| Calibration     | Final technical tuning          |

Important architectural constraint, stated explicitly: this is not meant to become hundreds of independent “ball classes.” The combination space can be enormous while the actual decisions presented to the player stay understandable — see Section 35's “four questions” for how that's kept manageable.

3\. Mechanical Foundation: Cobblemon Modular Poké Balls

Confirms and deepens Part 5's existing lean toward this mod as the ball system's base. Investigated feature set: 25 lid designs, 16 colors, independently customizable top/bottom sections, 6 core tiers, configurable catch rates, a dedicated Modular Ball Workbench (with slots for top lid/bottom lid/rim/button/core and a live preview), and Element Balls using Cobblemon Type Gems (now Affinity Gems, per Part 3's rename). Explicit caution preserved directly: don't simply rename the mod's existing mechanics and call that the E.R. system — use it as the mechanical foundation, then build E.R.'s own progression/lore/Resonance layer on top of it.

Direct system tie-in confirmed via a later sweep (Part 6): the Modular Ball Workbench itself is proposed as an Awakened Machine under the Resonant Transformation system, rather than an isolated custom workstation — Early: discover/rebuild basic Poké Ball manufacturing → Mid: learn specialized ball construction → Late: Awaken the Workbench with technology, magic, Nature's Aura, faction knowledge, and Resonance. See Part 6 for the full Resonant Transformation framework this plugs into.

Capture-power core tiers (as investigated in the mod)

|             |                              |
|-------------|------------------------------|
| **Core**    | **Approx. capture strength** |
| Copper      | 1×                           |
| Iron        | 1.5×                         |
| Gold        | 2×                           |
| Diamond     | 3×                           |
| Netherite   | 5×                           |
| Nether Star | Guaranteed                   |

Key E.R. design decision layered on top: capture strength should not be the ball's entire identity — two balls can share similar capture power while serving completely different purposes.

4\. Attunement Core (confirms Part 5)

This section independently confirms what's already documented in Part 5 — good consistency check, no contradiction found. Historical term: Resonance Core, used for the specialized type component. Renamed to Attunement Core once “Resonance Ball” was also in active use as a distinct concept and the overlap became confusing. Final distinction: Core = how strongly the ball captures; Attunement Core = what type/ecological Affinity the ball is aligned with; Treatment = what special function it performs; Resonance = how the ball interacts with its target/the world.

🕒 RESOLVED (Sept 2026, cross-referenced from Part 5): the Legendary Attunement Core (Personal Affinity Slot 5 unlock item) is confirmed a DIFFERENT, unrelated item from this ball-component family — a naming collision, not a shared family member. A rename for the Slot 5 item is recommended before implementation to avoid the collision going forward; see Part 5 for detail.

5\. Resonance Ball / Affinity Ball — Terminology Evolution (3 versions, preserved honestly)

This is the single messiest naming thread in the whole project, and it's being preserved as an honest multi-version history rather than silently flattened into one “correct” answer, per the Archive Preservation Principle.

|             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Version** | **Structure**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| V1          | Resonance Ball (neutral base) → Resonance Attunement (process) → Fire Resonance Ball (finished product)                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| V2          | Resonance Ball (neutral base) → Attainment (process) → Affinity Ball (finished product, e.g. Fire/Water/Ghost/Fairy Affinity Ball), with Attunement Core as the enabling component. Favored because “Resonance” describes the underlying force/process while “Affinity” describes the resulting relationship. |
| V3          | Modular Ball → Attunement Core → Attuned Ball, with “Resonance Ball” repurposed to mean the functional/gameplay designation for a ball actively being used in resonance with its target, rather than a product name.                                                                                          |

Best-supported current reading (still not unanimous in the source): Resonance Ball = neutral/base resonance-capable platform → Attainment/Resonance Attainment = the conversion process → Affinity Ball = the finished, type-aligned product → Attunement Core = the physical component enabling it all. Status: 🟡 Candidate — explicitly flagged in the recovery itself as needing a final terminology lock, not something to treat as already decided.

🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): RESOLVES the terminology ambiguity above. ‘Resonance Ball’ is confirmed as the true top-level umbrella — not a specific product tier, not one option among several, but the name of the entire technology family. Both existing sub-families sit under it: AFFINITY BALLS (built from an Attunement/Resonance Core) and ANOMALY BALLS (built from an Anomaly Core, CLR-0164). The shared name is earned honestly, not just convenient — every ball in the family resonates and tunes to its specific core and applied conditions, which is the literal mechanism both sub-families already share (CLR-0165). All Resonance Balls are products of a single named R&D institution, the MODULAR BALL PROGRAM — giving every ball in the family a genuine shared origin (same underlying technology, same research program) rather than an arbitrary shared name.

🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): shared baseline + unique perks, mirroring vanilla Pokémon's own ball design

Every Resonance Ball has two layers of behavior, not one flat capture-rate number: a BASELINE PERK SET shared by every ball in the family (earned by virtue of shared core technology — exact contents not yet designed, but should read as ‘what any Resonance Ball can do because it IS one,’ not situational), plus a small number of UNIQUE PERKS specific to that ball's particular Core/Attunement/Treatment combination. This directly mirrors the real design pattern already present in vanilla/Cobblemon balls (Quick Ball's early-turn bonus, Timer Ball's late-battle bonus, Dive Ball's underwater bonus, Dusk Ball's darkness bonus) — same tech, different area of effect, which is the exact framing Wesley gave for why this makes sense: they were built with the same underlying technology, just different materials, so the overall purpose stays constant while the execution/area of influence differs per ball.

🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): vanilla/mod ball absorption strategy — a direct application of No Best Ball at the pool level, not just per-ball design

Rather than letting vanilla Poké Balls and mod-added balls (Quick Ball, Timer Ball, Dusk Ball, Heavy Ball, Nest Ball, Lure Ball, Dive Ball, Net Ball, Repeat Ball, Beast Ball, and similar) sit as a separate, disconnected pool alongside the new Resonance Ball system, their standout single-mechanic identities get folded INTO the Resonance Ball system as Treatments or unique perks on specific attuned variants — then the original separate ball items are RETIRED rather than kept redundantly alongside their absorbed replacement. This is explicitly framed as fulfilling the already-locked No Best Ball principle at the POOL level, not just individual ball design: eliminates the ‘what do I even choose’ decision paralysis of two overlapping systems doing similar jobs, and lets fan-favorite mechanics survive as system components without requiring players to hold two near-identical items side by side. The Modular Ball Program becomes the single place all ball technology in the pack lives — base-mod balls included — rather than being an addition running parallel to an untouched vanilla ball pool.

*🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): the Master Ball (and Poké/Great/Ultra) are explicitly exempt from the absorption strategy above — the three base balls remain as a fixed, unmodified control group with no situational conditions, precisely so every Resonance Ball's bonus can be judged against a stable baseline. The Master Ball is kept too, but recontextualized rather than left as an arbitrary 100% stat: it is the MASTERWORK tier of the Resonance Ball system specifically, reusing the exact top tier already defined in the Resonant Transformation ladder (Part 6 — ‘Masterwork: Endgame hybrid technology’). Its guaranteed catch is earned in-world as a genuine amalgamation — built containing a sample of every Core tier, every Attunement type, every Treatment family, and Anomaly containment technology at once — rather than simply declaring a number. This also preserves No Best Ball in practice despite nominally being the best ball: building one requires having already explored and gathered from the entire system, so reaching it means the player has already engaged with every other ball family first, not skipped past them.*

*Open implementation work, not yet designed: the specific mapping of which vanilla/mod ball mechanics become which Treatments vs. unique Core/Attunement-tier perks, and whether absorption happens all at once or ball-by-ball as each is evaluated.*

6\. The Attainment/Attunement Process

Regardless of final naming, the process itself is consistent across all three terminology versions — explicitly identified as a C.O.C. example: Manufacture a neutral Resonance Ball → Select an intended Affinity → Prepare the ball → Expose it to an appropriate Resonance source → Allow the Affinity to align → Stabilize it → Produce the specialized Affinity Ball. Explicitly not 18 identical recipes with different colors — different Affinities can have different physical/ritual exposure methods:

|              |                                                                                |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Affinity** | **Example exposure method**                                                    |
| Fire         | Intense heat, Fire Aura, a furnace/forge, Fire Pokémon, Fire-related materials |
| Water        | Flowing water, an aqueduct, Water Pokémon, an aquatic environment              |
| Grass        | Healthy vegetation, Nature's Aura, living plants, Grass Pokémon                |
| Electric     | Create power generation, lightning, charged components, Electric Pokémon       |
| Ghost        | Occultism, spirits, soul-related materials, haunted locations                  |

7\. World Affinity Integration

The ball affects the world, not just the Pokémon inside it. Loop: Ball manufacture → Affinity alignment → Capture → World Affinity contribution → Ecological restoration → More Pokémon/phenomena become available. Hierarchy of contribution size: normal capture (small increase) \< appropriately attuned Modular Ball (enhanced increase) \< specialized treatment (alternative ecological/research/Resonance benefits) \< major restoration (dramatically larger increase) — explicitly designed so catching 1,000 Pokémon can't substitute for actually restoring the world.

World state can also gate ball manufacture quality, not just spawn availability: e.g. at 37 Fire World Affinity, Fire balls are possible but limited/weak; as Fire restoration progresses (37→60→80→100), attunement quality/availability improves. The player isn't just reading a number — they're interacting with the world that produces it. Status: 🟢 Strong reconstruction for the whole section; specific thresholds illustrative.

8\. Treatments

A completed Modular Ball can receive a Treatment for additional functionality, avoiding the need for every special function to be a fully separate ball. Recovered candidate families (explicitly marked as design candidates, not a locked list):

| **Family**              | **Example Treatments**                                                            |
| Natural (Nature's Aura) | Verdant, Aquatic, Floral, Ancient Grove, Conservation                             |
| Arcane (Ars Nouveau)    | Resonance, Dream, Fairy Attunement, Psychic Attunement, Dimensional Stabilization |
| Occult (Occultism)      | Spirit Binding, Umbral Containment, Soul Stabilization, Spectral Resonance        |
| Industrial (Create)     | Reinforced Shell, Precision Mechanism, Rapid Deployment, Containment Stabilizer   |
| Scientific (Research)   | Genetic Calibration, Species Recognition, Anomaly Stabilization, Research Capture |

Explicit purpose: prevent the system from becoming an 18-types × 10-effects × 6-cores × 25-appearances mechanical spreadsheet. Player-facing decisions are meant to stay at exactly four: Appearance, Core, Treatment, Purpose — see Section 15.

10\. Anomaly Balls

A structurally distinct category from Affinity Balls — not a stronger Poké Ball, but containment for entities whose behavior doesn't conform to ordinary capture: Paradox Pokémon, Ultra Beasts, Shadow Pokémon, Fractured Pokémon, dimensional entities, temporal anomalies.

|                                         |                                               |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| **Resonance-oriented capture**          | **Anomaly containment**                       |
| “What does this Pokémon resonate with?” | “Why is this entity behaving incorrectly?”    |
| World Affinity                          | Instability/anomaly                           |
| Type/ecological relationship            | Stabilization/containment                     |
| Fire, Water, Ghost, etc.                | Temporal, Dimensional, Shadow, Fracture, etc. |

Recovered candidates: Shadow Ball, Fracture Ball, Dimensional Ball, Temporal Ball, Paradox Ball — explicitly conceptual, not locked. Worked examples: a Temporal Stabilization Ball could reduce temporal instability during capture, record research, and potentially help resolve the anomaly; Dimensional Containment suits an Ultra Beast; Corruption Stabilization suits a Shadow Pokémon. Governing rule: the containment problem determines the ball configuration.

*🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): the ANOMALY CORE is the mechanism that fulfills the anti-category-sprawl guardrail above. Exactly mirroring how an Attunement Core (formerly Resonance Core) slots into the modular Lid/Core/Treatment architecture to produce a standard Affinity Ball, an Anomaly Core slots into the SAME architecture to produce an Anomaly Ball — same base item family, same construction pattern, no separate Anomaly-specific ball system required. The five recovered candidate names above (Shadow, Fracture, Dimensional, Temporal, Paradox) stop being five separate items and become either Anomaly Core variants (a Temporal Anomaly Core, a Dimensional Anomaly Core, etc.) or Treatment choices layered on a single generic Anomaly Core — exact split not yet decided, but either resolves the “47 categories to memorize” problem the same way. This is the concrete answer to that guardrail's ‘later direction,’ not a new direction competing with it.*

The ER Ball — supersedes the earlier GS Ball reinterpretation proposal, gives the Ritual Legendary-eligibility path its first physical worked example

LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): rather than reinterpreting the GS Ball directly, C.E.R. gets its own mysterious-key-item lineage native to the Eeveelutional Resonance research line — the ER Ball. Origin: partway through Eeveelutional Resonance research, researchers realize ordinary Poké Balls interfere with what they're trying to measure (a Pokémon's resonance state), and build an experimental containment device meant to PRESERVE and MEASURE resonance rather than simply capture. E.R. = Eeveelutional Resonance in-world; the name is a genuine in-fiction abbreviation, not just a project codename repurposed. Canon research-note joke worth keeping: 'The designation \u2018ER Ball\u2019 was intended as an abbreviation for Eeveelutional Resonance Ball. It has subsequently resulted in several researchers assuming the letters stand for something considerably more mysterious.'

Three-stage evolution, giving it a real quest arc rather than a single unlock: Prototype ER Ball (experimental, unstable, primarily research equipment, may have no conventional capture bonus at all) → ER Ball (properly stabilized, can interact with Affinity/Resonance states, stores resonance information) → ER Ball Mk. II / Resonance Ball (the mature, standardized technology once the underlying principles are understood). This gives the already-locked Resonance Ball umbrella name (CLR-0166) a genuine origin story: the ER Ball is its historical prototype, not two unrelated names competing for the same slot.

*This is what actually fulfills the Ritual Legendary-eligibility path's need for a physical worked example (Part 11, eligibility architecture) — the ER Ball's research-driven, mystery-object identity naturally extends toward becoming a summoning/ritual key for a specific Legendary or Mythical the same way GS Ball is inseparable from Celebi, without needing to reskin GS Ball directly. Supersedes the earlier proposal (never actually executed/locked) to reinterpret GS Ball itself for this purpose — the ER Ball accomplishes the same design goal with a stronger, more C.E.R.-native identity.*

*🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): HOW a Core becomes typed — resolves the crafting-UX fork between pre-typed components (craft a ‘Shadow Core’ directly) and a universal blank component attuned afterward. Answer: universal blanks, attuned as a separate step, for BOTH core families. The (Resonance/Attunement, exact final name still Candidate above) Core is a single generic, untyped item — raw Affinity gems/Essence are applied to it afterward, in a distinct Attunement action, to produce a typed result. The Anomaly Core works identically: one generic, untyped item, attuned afterward to a specific anomaly category (Shadow, Fracture, Dimensional, Temporal, Paradox). Player mental model for both: ‘I need a Core, then I attune it’ — not ‘I need to go find the specific typed Core for this job.’ Reasoning: matches ‘Attunement’ as a process verb rather than an object name, matches the pack's standing multi-stage-crafting house style (Resonant Transformation), and better serves the already-locked No Best Ball principle — a player holding blank Cores can decide what to attune them to in the moment rather than needing to correctly predict needs back at the crafting bench.*

*🕒 LOCKED (Wesley, Sept 2026): where an Anomaly Core actually comes from — not a separate raw material, but a distorted/unstable version of a Resonance Core itself. Reuses existing terminology directly rather than inventing new vocabulary: ‘Distorted’ is the exact term already locked for the low end of the World Affinity population-shift scale (Part 3, 0–20 ‘Distorted Ecosystem,’ Twisted Forms dominant). A Resonance Core exposed to sufficient instability — low-Affinity conditions, proximity to a genuine anomaly, or similar — becomes an Anomaly Core, giving the two Core families one shared origin rather than two disconnected material chains. This also supplies real narrative logic for why Anomaly Balls work as containment at all: they are built from material that has already gone through the same kind of instability the entity being contained is experiencing — like genuinely answering to like, not an arbitrary separate technology.*

Explicit architectural guardrail against category sprawl (Resonance/Anomaly/Research/Conservation/Faction/etc. balls each becoming their own item family — “47 different ball categories the player has to memorize”): later direction makes Resonance Ball the broad architectural concept, with configurations/Treatments underneath it, Anomaly containment included.

11\. Type Gems / Affinity Gems & the Ball System

Originally considered as the literal “Resonance Core” before that term moved to Attunement Core (Section 4) — e.g. a Fire Gem enabling improved Fire capture, Fire research, Fire Pokémon compatibility, reduced capture instability in hot environments, Personal Fire Affinity, and Fire-starter progression; a Ghost Gem interacting with Ghost Pokémon, Occultism, Shadow phenomena, haunted structures, and death-related discoveries.

Open resource-economy question, not locked: whether Affinity Gems should be finite/crystallized manifestations of Resonance (sourced from the world's actual ecological state — Restoration → Resonance becomes available → crystallizes → usable material → advanced technology) rather than a casually mass-producible commodity like iron. A major proposed direction, not a locked resource lifecycle.

12\. Personal Affinity Guardrail for Balls

An explicit design caution, worth its own entry since it refines Part 1's Personal Affinity system: high Trainer Affinity should NOT directly translate into raw catch-rate bonuses (“My Fire Affinity is 100, therefore my Fire Ball catches better”) — that would recreate a simple linear power hierarchy and undercut build diversity. Instead, high Personal Affinity should grant familiarity and knowledge: better information about that type's Pokémon, improved research, behavioral/environmental feedback, and access to more advanced Treatments for that Affinity — while a Water specialist can still use a Fire ball just fine, only without the specialist's edge. Status: 🕒 Locked — stated as an explicit guardrail, not a suggestion.
